paper.title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
paper.abstract: Increased computing power has transformed computational science and improved predictive capabilities for complex systems, but many phenomena still exceed current simulation capabilities or require rapid evaluations for fast design iterations. Closure models address this challenge by approximating unresolved effects in reduced or incomplete dynamical systems. Data-driven closures offer a flexible mechanism for improving model accuracy and applicability, but approaches that embed the closure within a computational model for construction and training phases can be computationally expensive and cause numerical instabilities in the computational model during training. To avoid the challenges posed by embedded approaches, staged approaches to closure-model learning have been developed. The first stage uses data assimilation to infer state and closure trajectories from observations. The second stage trains a machine learning closure model offline using the assimilated data, thereby avoiding repeated simulator calls during training. In this work, we investigate the cost and accuracy tradeoffs between embedded and staged data-driven closure modeling approaches for a synthetic epidemiological SIQR model with a nonlinear state-dependent quarantine closure. The results illustrate a practical accuracy-efficiency trade-off: for this exemplar, embedded training provides the strongest average accuracy, while the staged approach yields comparable qualitative behavior with a moderate increase in error, substantially fewer model evaluations, and improved optimization robustness.

paper.title: New classes of reversible cellular automata
paper.abstract: Cellular automata find applications in cryptography, error correction, theoretical computer science, and the simulation of physical and biological processes. We say that a Boolean function is a proper lifting if its induced cellular automaton is reversible. This paper introduces new classes of proper liftings, constructed through compositions of landscape functions, and explores their cryptographic potential by computing indicators relevant to differential and linear cryptanalysis. We combine theoretical and computational methods to obtain a complete classification of proper liftings for diameters up to $6$. Several open problems and conjectures are posed along the way.

paper.title: Distributed Adaptive Estimation with ISS Guarantees for Sensor Networks with Partially Unknown Source Dynamics
paper.abstract: This paper studies distributed adaptive estimation over sensor networks with partially unknown source dynamics. We present parallel continuous-time and discrete-time designs in which each node runs a local adaptive observer and exchanges information over a directed graph. For both time scales, we establish stability of the network coupling operators, prove boundedness of all internal signals, and show convergence of each node's estimate to the source despite model uncertainty and disturbances. We further derive input-to-state stability (ISS) bounds that quantify robustness to bounded process noise. A key distinction is that the discrete-time design uses constant adaptive gains and per-step regressor normalization to handle sampling effects, whereas the continuous-time design does not. A unified Lyapunov framework links local observer dynamics with graph topology. Simulations on star, cyclic, and path networks corroborate the analysis, demonstrating accurate tracking, robustness, and scalability with the number of sensing nodes.

paper.title: Circular orders: topology and continuous actions
paper.abstract: We study the topology of circularly ordered sets. While the algebraic notion is classical, the general topological theory has received comparatively little attention. In this work we provide a self-contained topological exposition and present several new directions and results. Our aim is to initiate a systematic study of generalized circularly ordered topological spaces and of continuous group actions on them. Provide a convex uniform structure description of circularly ordered compactifications. This yields a topological analysis of Novak's regular completion and its uniformity. Demonstrate that this uniform-structure approach yields several new results in the theory of $G$-compactifications for topological group actions on abstract ordered spaces. Reexamine functions of bounded variation on circularly ordered sets and prove generalizations of Helly's selection theorem (for circular and linear orders). These developments and the systematic analysis of circular order topologies are motivated by recent applications in topological dynamics, particularly in joint works with Eli Glasner.

paper.title: Wave number dynamics in the real and complex Ginzburg-Landau equations
paper.abstract: We investigate the large-scale dynamics of the one-dimensional real and complex Ginzburg-Landau equations using a scalar equation for the local wave number derived by a Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) expansion. For the real equation, the reduction has a conserved gradient structure. With higher-order regularization, we obtain families of exact stationary solutions and show that all nonuniform steady states are linearly unstable. These include localized holes distinct from the classical Langer-Ambegaokar hole. In the Eckhaus-unstable regime, the reduced equation develops finite-time singularities associated with phase slips. We derive a universal self-similar description of this process, with parameter-independent scaling exponents in good agreement with direct numerical simulations. The similarity profile satisfies a nonlinear fourth-order boundary-value problem admitting multiple numerically identified solutions. For the complex equation with nearly real coefficients, an additional Burgers-type nonlinearity produces wave steepening and traveling shocks connecting plane waves of different wave numbers. We derive the shock profile exactly and show numerically that the full complex Ginzburg-Landau equation converges to this prediction in the appropriate asymptotic limit. Outside this regime, the wave number profile becomes nonmonotonic, as explained in terms of spatial dynamics. These shocks differ qualitatively from classical Nozaki-Bekki solutions. The reduced equation thus unifies stationary holes, self-similar collapse toward phase slips, and propagating shocks within a common description of pattern-forming systems.

paper.title: Cost of one-relator groups
paper.abstract: For any infinite one-relator group $\Gamma=\langle S \mid w^m\rangle$, we prove that $\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma)=|S|-\frac{1}{m}$. For such groups, this gives $\beta^{(2)}_1(\Gamma)=\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma) - 1$, answering a special case of Gaboriau's question on the relationship between cost and first $\ell^2$-Betti number.

paper.title: L2-L2-gain bounds for quadratic output systems
paper.abstract: We derive an explicit bound for the L2-L2-gain of linear time-invariant systems whose output is a quadratic function of the state and the input. Such systems appear naturally in many areas, for example for port-Hamiltonian systems, optimal-control, and stochastic problems. In case the output is purely quadratic in the state, the bound is determined by the supremum over $\omega\in\mathbb R$ of the L2-norms of the bivariate transfer function restricted to the anti-diagonals $\{(s,\, i\omega-s)\mid s\in i\mathbb R\}$ of the frequency domain $i\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R $. Further, we show how the bound can be computed by solving linear matrix equations. This result provides a practical tool for assessing and reducing quadratic-output models.

paper.title: One Shot, Twenty-One Balls: A Computer-Assisted Proof of a Single-Stroke Total Clearance in an Idealized Model of Snooker
paper.abstract: Snooker folklore holds that no single stroke can pocket all twenty-one object balls. We examine the claim in an explicit model: twenty-two equal disks on a rectangle with six pocket points, under constant rolling deceleration, frictionless collisions with normal restitution, and lossy specular cushions. We exhibit a configuration and a stroke, and prove in interval arithmetic that every stroke in an explicit box around it pockets all twenty-one object balls, so the set of successful strokes has positive measure. That set is a ribbon: every speed from 9.3213 to 12 m/s works, while the certified window of directions is 9.4813e-43 radians wide, a number explained by a first-order analysis of twenty near-grazing collisions. A second configuration, a near-frozen cluster, has a certified window 9.4e-4 radians wide, thirty-nine orders of magnitude wider; its certificate uses Taylor models of degree six. The strokes with a given list of events form a semialgebraic set, and the endpoints of the windows are algebraic numbers. For the regulation opening position we state the corresponding conjecture, and show that if it holds with a regular witness then a finite certified search establishes it.

paper.title: Density of the multidimensional Lagrange spectrum
paper.abstract: The Lagrange spectrum is a classical object in number theory, defined as the set of values of $\liminf_{q\to\infty} q\, \mathrm{dist}(q\alpha,\mathbb{Z})$ where $\alpha$ runs through irrational numbers. It has a complicated structure, with the discrete part, Hall's ray, and a transitional part in between. One can similarly define Lagrange spectrum in the multidimensional set-up, and until now not much has been understood about it. In this paper we prove that, unlike in the one-dimensional case, the closure of the multidimensional Lagrange spectrum is equal to the interval between $0$ and its supremum. The proof relies on a correspondence between Diophantine approximation and dynamics on the space of unimodular lattices and proceeds by studying a dynamical counterpart of the Lagrange spectrum that we call dynamical Lagrange spectrum. The latter is shown to be equal to the interval between $0$ and its maximum by means of an argument utilizing the higher rank nature of the set-up. A passage from full dynamical spectrum to the density of the Diophantine spectrum is achieved by applying equidistribution of expanding translates of horospheres in the space of lattices.
